correctness.rationale: The full proof gives two exact universal Rayleigh certificates: a convex blend of orthogonal mean-zero modes when 0<d<=3, and a single path-mode witness when d>=3. Explicit allocations attain each bound. Equalities in the witnesses force all optimizers, including potentially nonsymmetric allocations, and spectral block analysis proves Fiedler multiplicities. The critical d=3 segment and both endpoint cases are addressed. The standalone proof checker passed 12 symbolic identities, 27 exact-rational four-by-four spectra, four critical configurations and 1440 exact rational competitor-certificate checks. The computation does not replace the all-real-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The four-cycle is the smallest nontriangular network admitting competing routes; a single exceptional physical edge price is the smallest heterogeneous-cost perturbation of its symmetric design. The complete exact phase law shows when the costly edge is useful, locates the ninefold deletion threshold, and classifies a surprising nonunique critical face and a Fiedler multiplicity change. These are structural design and SDP-benchmark facts, not a selected arbitrary numerical slice or a uniform-cost recomputation. The result is intentionally limited to this first nontrivial cycle and does not claim a larger general-cycle theorem.
